channel.title: SECOND TAKE (English)
channel.description: Long-form interviews with founders and executives about what they chose after the first take went wrong: shutting down, starting over, stepping away.

item.title: Her father ran the line for 40 years. As his successor, she shut it down
item.description: Three years after she took over, orders for their main product — auto parts — had halved. What remained: craftsmen who’d worked for her father, and a production line losing money.

item.title: He started the company with his best friend from college. Then he asked him to leave
item.description: Two founders, equal titles, equal shares. By the time they had 30 employees, nobody could make the final call.

item.title: He left to protect it: 143 days to walk away from the company he founded
item.description: He believed nothing would move without him — until he admitted that he was the one holding the company back.

item.title: She knew it would fail. It still took her a year to stop
item.description: The losses grew every month, and so did the messages from customers who believed in the product. Every signal said stop. She rewrote her own exit criteria three times.

item.title: The morning after he decided to close the company, he couldn’t say a word
item.description: Revenue had fallen by two-thirds, and the cash would last two more months. He came in to announce the shutdown — and found his team had spent the night writing a rescue plan.
